corpus: original model suggestions with verified insertion in earlier sessions
finding: No useful primary personal advantage is established. Useful advantage remains unresolved against every primary rival under both interval methods. Primary pooled and donor comparisons favor personal adaptation at zero under writer resampling, but neither clears the useful margin or survives crossed writer/prompt resampling at zero. Primary base and uniform intervals include zero under both methods. Adapted-minus-base donor useful advantage is excluded under writer resampling but remains unresolved under crossed resampling; pooled advantage remains unresolved under both. Residual uniform useful advantage is excluded under both methods, with every residual interval including zero. Raw sums retain useful base, pooled and donor uncertainty under both methods. The raw donor comparison favors personal adaptation at zero only under writer resampling, without clearing the useful margin or surviving crossed resampling; raw base and pooled intervals include zero. Raw sums are worse than uniform under both methods. No parity follows.
limits: Repeated selected model text adds training passes, not personal evidence. Suggestion supply and selection provenance, sparse histories, fixed donor/global training, shared exposed units and changed corpus support preclude epoch/backbone/corpus rankings, independent human confirmation, population limits, private-goal inference or a whole-matrix verdict. Historical failures and unknown attempts stay separate; no new retry.
